topics.topic: Operation-element conclusion after not_applied and before a fresh approval
questions: What exact conclusion must `effects.operation_element_conclusion` return during recovery for an attempt resolved `not_applied`?

After `resolve_unknown_outcome` records `not_applied` but before a fresh approval exists, what conclusion must `effects.operation_element_conclusion` return so that `run_graph.plan_run` knows whether the element is waiting or ready to be reached?

What must `effects.operation_element_conclusion` return after an `outcome_unknown` NodeExecution's attempt is resolved `not_applied`, before a fresh approval has been requested? A11 rule 3 calls it waiting for `owner_approval`, while the changed recovery text calls it not reached and ready, and the public conclusion API permits `not reached` only when no NodeExecution exists.

quotes:
Its conclusion: succeeded with outputs; failed with its status, or with
`applied_outputs_unknown` for an attempt resolved applied whose binding has
outputs; waiting with its reason and, for `owner_approval`, the `approval_id`
of the element's `requested` approval, so `runs` builds the run's answer
(Conventions) without reading approval records itself; or not reached when the
element has no NodeExecution yet (A11 rule 3).

`not_applied`: the element waits again with reason `owner_approval`, and the
     next send, under a fresh approval even where a grant exists (K-08), is the
     next attempt.
judgement.why: State 5 permits not reached only when no NodeExecution exists, while A11 requires the resolved element, whose outcome_unknown NodeExecution remains, to wait for owner approval.

topics.topic: Which decided approval outcomes make an element ready during recovery
questions: Which approval decisions make the element ready during recovery?
Does “approval was decided” mean only an approval decided `approved`, or how must recovery distinguish `approved` from `refused` here?
Does “approval was decided” mean only `approved`, or also `refused`? A refused approval already has a `refused_by_owner` NodeExecution and must end the run rather than make the element ready.

quotes:
an
operation element whose wait no longer holds (its approval decided, its attempt
resolved `not_applied`) is not reached and so is ready, which leaves its run
`running`; then advances, as the kernel, every run left `running`, reaching
every ready element while others still wait (A13 rule 8, A14 rule 5).
a `refused_by_owner` record ends the run `refused` (A10 rule 3).
judgement.why: The recovery passage treats every decided approval as making the element ready, while the run-graph operation requires a refused approval's record to end the run refused.

topics.topic: Result returned by read_runner_report for malformed, partial, or oversized reports
questions: What exact result does `read_runner_report` return when framing is invalid, the report is partial, or the channel bound is exceeded, so that `sandbox` can apply the A03 outcome order?

What does `read_runner_report` return when the channel bound is exceeded or the report is unreadable or partial? Its Outputs list has no malformed-report result and its Errors section says none, yet `sandbox` needs an explicit result to classify the execution.

quotes: read_runner_report: [BEHAVIOR] The program writes each message as one line of UTF-8 JSON ended by a newline, an object whose kind is trap (with the trapped name), resource, crashed (with failure, the exception's type and message or null) or returned (with is_dict and outputs, each port, form, json_text and contents, the bytes base64-encoded). read_runner_report MUST decode the lines in order: trap names in the order written, resource_hit true when any resource line is present, crashed and failure from a crashed line, returned only from one complete returned line; a line that is not complete JSON of a known kind, the last line cut short included, ends the decoding and what follows is ignored.

read_runner_report: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns RunnerReport with trap_hits, resource_hit, crashed, failure and returned (None when no complete returned line was read), each ReturnedOutput's json_text set only for form json and contents holding the file's bytes, or the list's in order, only for file and file_list.

execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] MUST write into the exchange directory the runner_source text, the code, and every input — a value port's canonical JSON, a file port's bytes, a many file port one file per element in list order — and start the interpreter on the runner file with the runner_arguments of a RunnerLaunch naming those files by their paths inside the environment, the output ports, the bounds and the channel's descriptor number; it MUST close its own copy of the channel's write end once bubblewrap has started, read the channel while the environment runs until it closes, and decode what it read with read_runner_report. It reads at most eight times bounds.output_bytes plus 1 048 576 bytes (room for base64, JSON escaping, trap lines and the failure); when the runner writes more it stops reading, kills the environment as for its wall deadline, decodes what it read and observes channel_over_bound, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted. The parent sets no setrlimit limit: there the process limit would count every process of the user on the host and bubblewrap could not create its namespace (EAGAIN).
judgement.why: The later notes define malformed or partial input as a RunnerReport with no returned value unless a complete returned message was decoded, and classify an over-bound channel separately as resource_exhausted.

topics.topic: Whether resolving an attempt as not_applied immediately re-reaches the element
questions: After an attempt is resolved `not_applied`, what conclusion must the element expose to the advance, and must that same request immediately call `effects.reach_operation_element`?

Does `continue_after_resolution` merely record the resolution and enter the ordinary advance loop, or does it itself reach the resolved element before that loop? The phrase says both that it is not reached and that it is reached again, while A11 rule 3 still says the kernel reaches it in the owner's same request.

quotes:
Its conclusion: succeeded with outputs; failed with its status, or with
`applied_outputs_unknown` for an attempt resolved applied whose binding has
outputs; waiting with its reason and, for `owner_approval`, the `approval_id`
of the element's `requested` approval, so `runs` builds the run's answer
(Conventions) without reading approval records itself; or not reached when the
element has no NodeExecution yet (A11 rule 3).

the element is not reached any more, so the advance reaches it again through
`effects.reach_operation_element`, which runs the pre-send checks and, finding
no authority, requests that approval for the request as built now (A11 rule 3).
judgement.why: The advance text requires the resolved element to expose not reached even though the public conclusion operation restricts that result to an element with no NodeExecution.

topics.topic: Accepted source variants and behavior of record_flow_output
questions: Which source variants may `record_flow_output` receive, and what must it do for each? The text does not say whether it accepts only a mapped-list draft, the same three-way source union as `deliver_input`, or an already-written StoredValue reference as well.

topics.topic: In-memory representation returned for an unwritten mapped value list
questions: What exactly represents a value list before it is written? A StoredValue M21 is a stored record with a `value_id`, but this operation writes nothing, so callers cannot know whether they receive a draft record, canonical bytes and facts, or an already valid reference.

topics.topic: Ordering when plan_run produces both drafts and a ready node
questions: May one `plan_run` result contain both new drafts and a ready node, and if so must `runs` write the drafts before executing that node, execute first, or treat such a result as invalid? The choice changes trace/store order and recovery behavior.

topics.topic: Recovery state when a fresh approval request exists but its run-progress write was lost
questions: If `not_applied` was resolved and a fresh approval request was committed, but the following run-progress write was lost before restart, does recovery preserve the existing `owner_approval` wait or treat the element as ready and reach it again?

topics.topic: Representation, identity, and disclosure class of mapped file lists
questions: What model value or reference represents a mapped file list, especially an empty one, and where is its disclosure class carried? M23 names files through individual SpooledFile facts, while an empty list has no SpooledFile from which its class or identity can be recovered.

topics.topic: Selection and ordering of mapped-list ceiling failures when several outputs are oversized
questions: When more than one delivered output list exceeds the ceiling, what must `assemble_mapped_lists` return, and in what output-port order is the reported list selected?

topics.topic: plan_run representation of a recordless aggregate-node failure
questions: How does `plan_run` represent this recordless aggregate-node failure—including its status/detail—so dependants become `upstream_failed`, the run becomes `failed`, and readers derive the same explanation?
